transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-13 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Priya Nair, Jordan Brooks, Maya Lopez, Elliot Rivers + company-wide attendees (chat truncated)

Summary (auto): Q4 beat plan on ARR growth, product milestones delivered, new risks around capacity planning for Dedicated, prepping SOC2 re-audit in Q1.

Topics: Q4 results, Dedicated and Private launches, Redwood Optimize beta, hiring/org updates, security & audits.

Action items (auto): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hi everyone, happy, uh, happy Monday — sorry, Tuesday — happy Tuesday. Thanks for joining the December all-hands. We have a bunch to cover so I want to keep it tight, we'll do the high-level, then Priya will go into product and engineering, Jordan on go-to-market and ops, and then open up to Q&A.

[00:34] Priya Nair: Cool, thanks Samir. Quick product highlights: Dedicated GA went out to the first set of customers last month, latency SLOs are holding at the 95th percentile we published, so that's good news. We also shipped the private control plane preview; a couple confusing notes — some customers reported firewall/NAT edge cases, so engineering is triaging. There's also the Redwood Optimise beta — sorry, Optimize — that's in limited beta with five customers, early results show 12-20% token cost reduction on average depending on batch profiles.

[01:15] Jordan Brooks: On the revenue side, Q4 ARR was +18% vs plan which is, you know, we should celebrate that. New bookings were driven by two mid-market customers moving to Dedicated. On the flip side churn from lower-tier customers remained flat. We do need to watch pipeline coverage in EMEA as we ramp next quarter.

[01:47] Maya Lopez: A note on product roadmap: next quarter we're prioritizing three things — 1) Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity, 2) Private GA for VPC/on-prem, 3) Optimize improvements (more fine-grained quantization suggestions and better batching heuristics). We'll be shipping a roadmap doc this week.

[02:12] Elliot Rivers: Small engineering update — we're optimizing kernel selection for some model variants which has improved throughput on Ampere and Hopper-based instances. There was a slight mis-transcription in the release notes where KV cache was written as K-V cash, so, uh, please ignore that. Also running a broader benchmark comparing NVLink vs non-NVLink setups — early numbers: NVLink helps for long context workloads, as expected.

[02:45] Speaker 1: Question from chat — "what's the plan for model rollouts and automatic fallbacks?"

[02:55] Priya Nair: Great question. The rollout story is canary + automatic fallback. If Dedicated can't meet latency SLOs we route to either a compatible quantized variant or to Hosted with data routing policies. We're also adding route-level tracing in Console so ops teams can see token-level latency and cost breakdowns.

[03:22] Samir Patel: Thanks. Security update? Jordan, do you want to cover SOC2 and audits?

[03:29] Jordan Brooks: Sure. We completed the remediation list from the last internal audit, and the external pre-audit is scheduled for early Jan. Key ask to teams: make sure your runbooks and deployment docs are up to date. KMS/HSM integrations were validated with two customers — some nit: a couple of our logging hooks were too verbose for PII controls, so we've gated them behind RBAC and audit-log filters.

[04:02] Maya Lopez: On compliance, product will produce a compliance checklist we can share with Sales for procurement calls. Also we'll link the security whitepaper and the SOC2 evidence guide in the #security-docs channel.

[04:25] Speaker 2 (from marketing): Any updates on the marketplace listings?

[04:30] Jordan Brooks: Yes, listing for our Dedicated offering is live in one cloud marketplace, working on two more regions. That should help enterprise adoption. Pricing guidance — we'll share a draft with revenue ops after today's meeting.

[04:50] Samir Patel: Quick note on hiring and org changes — we are not doing a broad hiring freeze, but we're tightening reqs on non-core roles. Engineering will still hire for critical infra and runtime roles. Jordan will share the updated org chart and hiring plan this week.

[05:12] Elliot Rivers: Also to add, we're moving a small number of infra-focused SREs into a central serving runtime team to accelerate kernel and batching work. This is a reorg, not headcount reduction. People impacted will be notified by EOD.

[05:35] Samir Patel: OK, let's move to questions. We'll try to get through as many as we can.

[05:40] [Audience Q] Speaker 3: For customers using Private on-prem, what's the upgrade story? Any downtime?

[05:46] Priya Nair: Good question. Private supports rolling upgrades with zero-downtime for most model-serving changes, we do recommend scheduling major infra upgrades in maintenance windows. There are a few edge cases during kernel ABI changes where a restart might be required, but we aim to minimize that. We'll publish the exact TL;DR in the Private playbook.

[06:20] Speaker 4: Are we supporting SAML SSO for Private GA?

[06:23] Jordan Brooks: Yes, SAML/SSO and RBAC support are in the Private GA checklist; we validated with one pilot customer. We also support KMS integrations and allow customer-managed keys for Private deployments.

[06:45] Speaker 5: Any competitor moves we should watch?

[06:48] Samir Patel: Nothing new major; major cloud vendors are improving managed endpoints but the differentiator for us is inference economics — latency/cost controls, predictable Dedicated pools, and the unified API across modes. Keep focusing on those messages.

[07:05] Maya Lopez: Quick product note — we're also shipping structured output improvements for function/tool calling which should make some of the developer integrations smoother in January.

[07:22] [Internal comment] Speaker 6: Someone in chat notes an odd transcription: "Red Wood" instead of "Redwood" — ignore.

[07:30] Samir Patel: Last section, OKRs for Q1 2027. High level: 1) Increase Dedicated revenue 2x, 2) Private GA and 5 pilot customers, 3) Reduce average token cost for hosted API by 15% via Optimize and batching, 4) SOC2 maintenance. Each lead will put a one-pager in the OKR doc repo by Friday.

[08:05] Priya Nair: Engineering priorities mapped to those OKRs: batching, kernel selection improvements, and deployment abstractions for Private. We'll refine capacity forecasting tools to avoid the kind of last-minute oversubscribe we saw in November.

[08:28] Samir Patel: Cool. Open floor — quick lightning questions.

[08:32] Speaker 7: Will we extend the beta for Optimize to more customers before GA?

[08:35] Maya Lopez: Yes, plan is to double the beta cohort in Jan, collect more promptset-driven evals, and have a pricing conversation mid-Jan.

[08:45] Speaker 8: Any updates on the Docs revamp?

[08:48] Elliot Rivers: Docs is in progress; new quickstart templates for Dedicated and Private land this week, and we have a docs sprint planned for Jan.

[09:02] Samir Patel: Alright team, thanks everyone. Important to close the loop on action items — Priya, Maya, Elliot, Jordan — please coordinate and update the threads. We'll follow up with the OKR one-pagers and the roadmap doc. Happy holidays to those taking time off, and we'll reconvene mid-Jan for a short strategy day.

[09:28] END

Notes on transcription: As with many Fireflies exports, there are occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (e.g., Redwood Optimise spelling, "K-V cash" for KV cache). The transcript preserves conversational style, interruptions, and chat references.
